_comment: Copy to holdings.json and fill in from primary sources.
Share counts come from SEC filings — Form 4, Schedule 13D/G and proxy
statements — not from a secondary list. Private stakes are hand-set marks
from the last funding round and should carry a date in your own notes.
icaoHex / tail go in ONLY once the aircraft is confirmed to the person.
Leave tailVerified false until you have that confirmation; the app shows an
'unverified' badge so an unchecked mapping never reads as fact.
socialUrl is a plain profile link (X, Bluesky, wherever they actually
post) — the app links out to it, it never embeds or polls live posts.
wikipediaTitle defaults to the name with spaces replaced by underscores;
set it only when that doesn't resolve to the right page (disambiguation,
a stage name, etc). The photo is pulled only if Wikipedia's own thumbnail
is hosted on Commons — Commons is free-license-only by policy, so a
non-free 'fair use' image (hosted locally on Wikipedia instead) never
makes it into the app; that person just gets the article link, no photo.
mmsi / vesselName go in ONLY once a yacht is confirmed to the person —
same bar as icaoHex/tail above, from public vessel registries and AIS
trackers (MarineTraffic, VesselFinder, etc), never guessed. Leave
vesselVerified false until you're sure; the app shows an 'unverified'
badge until it is. Also requires ais_listener.py running separately —
see backend/README section on vessels — this file alone isn't enough
to populate live vessel data, the same way icaoHex alone still needs
the ADS-B fetch to actually run.
birthDate is 'YYYY-MM-DD'. It's the one field here that's genuinely
static — the app computes age from it client-side, so it advances on
its own with no new snapshot required. residence is city/region only
('Starbase, TX'), never a street address, same granularity rule as the
flight/vessel location fields. Leave residence out entirely rather than
guess when public reporting is stale, conflicting, or describes a move
in progress rather than a settled address — an omitted field reads
honestly in the UI; a wrong one doesn't.
bio is one or two plain sentences: birthplace and the last school or
university actually attended, whether or not they finished it — same
sourcing bar and same static-fact treatment as birthDate/residence,
just prose instead of a single value, because several of these people
left a LATER graduate program unfinished after completing an earlier
degree elsewhere, and prose is the only honest way to say 'last
attended' without it reading as 'graduated from.' Leave it out rather
than write one until it's actually been researched — a missing bio
card is honest, a copied-from-a-stale-Wikipedia-lead one isn't.
edgarCik is that person's own SEC EDGAR reporting-owner CIK — NOT their
company's issuer CIK, a different number (musk's is 1494730; Tesla's is
1318605). Find it at data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK<guess>.json and check
the 'name' field actually matches before trusting it. Optional — leave it
out (like huang below) and edgar_check.py just skips that person rather
than guessing a CIK. When set, it's used by ../.github/workflows/edgar-
check.yml to periodically surface new Form 4 filings for review — see
edgar_check.py's docstring for why that script only ever reports a diff
rather than rewriting the holdings below itself.
